treatment_plan.summary: 67-year-old female with known non-valvular atrial fibrillation (CHA₂DS₂-VASc = 4) on warfarin (INR 2.4) status post successful PCI with drug-eluting stent for NSTEMI, with concurrent Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. This is a complex antithrombotic scenario requiring careful balancing of AF stroke prevention (OAC), acute coronary syndrome treatment (antiplatelet therapy), and post-DES stent thrombosis prevention. Triple therapy (VKA + aspirin + clopidogrel) is the initial recommended strategy with transition to dual therapy, with INR intensity reduction to 2.0–2.5 during triple therapy period.

recommendations.intervention: Warfarin — continue with reduced INR target range 2.0–2.5 during triple therapy period; return to INR 2.0–3.0 (target 2.5) after discontinuation of aspirin — essential for stroke prevention in AF with CHA₂DS₂-VASc 4
recommendations.rationale: Patient has CHA₂DS₂-VASc score of 4 (age 65–74, diabetes, female sex, vascular disease/NSTEMI) placing her at high thromboembolic risk; ongoing warfarin is mandatory. During VKA + clopidogrel + low-dose aspirin combination, INR intensity should be carefully regulated to 2.0–2.5 to minimise bleeding.

recommendations.intervention: Aspirin 75–100 mg daily orally — initial phase of triple therapy for 3–6 months post-ACS with DES, then discontinue — antiplatelet agent for acute coronary syndrome secondary prevention
recommendations.rationale: Following ACS with PCI in this 67F with AF, triple therapy (VKA, aspirin, clopidogrel) should be considered in the short term (3–6 months). Aspirin 75–100 mg daily is part of this triple regimen.
contraindications_checked: Warfarin interaction acknowledged — INR target reduced to 2.0–2.5 during triple therapy

recommendations.intervention: Clopidogrel 75 mg daily orally — as part of triple therapy for 3–6 months post-ACS with DES, then continue as long-term dual therapy with warfarin — ADP receptor antagonist for stent thrombosis prevention and ACS secondary prevention
recommendations.rationale: After the initial 3–6 months of triple therapy, the patient should transition to long-term VKA plus clopidogrel 75 mg daily (or alternatively aspirin 75–100 mg daily). Clopidogrel is the preferred P2Y12 inhibitor in this anticoagulated patient, as this guideline predates routine ticagrelor/prasugrel use in triple therapy with OAC.
contraindications_checked: Warfarin interaction acknowledged — careful INR regulation required

recommendations.intervention: Prasugrel 10 mg daily — alternative P2Y12 inhibitor more effective in diabetics; recommended after coronary angiography in high-risk patients undergoing PCI — ADP receptor antagonist
recommendations.rationale: This 67F has T2DM; prasugrel has been found to be more effective in diabetics undergoing PCI. However, prasugrel must be used with caution in the context of triple therapy with warfarin due to increased bleeding risk. Prasugrel is not recommended in patients >75 years old or with prior stroke/TIA — patient is 67 with no history of stroke, so age criterion is met.
contraindications_checked: Warfarin — triple therapy bleeding risk must be weighed
Weight >60 kg (not specified — to be confirmed)

recommendations.intervention: Ticagrelor 90 mg BD orally — alternative P2Y12 inhibitor shown to significantly reduce cardiovascular endpoints compared to clopidogrel in ACS; short-acting agent useful if surgery needed — ADP receptor antagonist
recommendations.rationale: Ticagrelor was shown to significantly reduce cardiovascular endpoints when compared to clopidogrel in patients with ACS. This agent is short acting and can be used in patients who may need surgery. However, potential drawbacks include dyspnoea and transient ventricular pauses. In this 67F with AF on warfarin, the higher bleeding risk with triple therapy must be considered.

recommendations.intervention: Statin therapy (e.g. Atorvastatin 80 mg daily or Simvastatin 40 mg daily) orally — high-potency statin initiated early and continued indefinitely — lipid modification for secondary prevention post-ACS
recommendations.rationale: Early initiation of high dose statin therapy soon after admission for UA/NSTEMI can reduce major adverse cardiac events. This 67F with NSTEMI and T2DM is at high CV risk and warrants aggressive lipid management. Per T2DM CPG, all patients over 40 should be treated with a statin regardless of baseline LDL-C.

recommendations.intervention: ACE inhibitor (e.g. Ramipril, starting 2.5 mg BD, target 10 mg daily) orally — initiated early in patients with diabetes and post-NSTEMI for cardioprotective and prognostic benefit
recommendations.rationale: ACE-I should be administered early for patients with LV dysfunction and diabetes. This 67F has T2DM and NSTEMI — ACE-I is indicated for long-term secondary prevention and recurrent ischaemia prevention.
contraindications_checked: No current ACE-I or ARB use noted

recommendations.intervention: Metformin — continue as first-line glucose-lowering therapy for Type 2 Diabetes — requires dose adjustment if eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m²; must be temporarily withheld if contrast nephropathy risk
recommendations.rationale: Metformin is the preferred first-line therapy for T2DM. Per the NSTEMI CPG (Appendix VII), nephrotoxic agents including metformin should be avoided during contrast exposure. This 67F requires ongoing metformin with renal function monitoring, especially post-PCI with contrast exposure.
contraindications_checked: Renal function (eGFR) — dose adjustment required if <60 mL/min/1.73m²
Contrast exposure during PCI — metformin avoidance around procedure

recommendations.intervention: Echocardiography — assess LV ejection fraction and wall motion abnormalities post-NSTEMI; guides need for ACE-I continuation, beta-blocker therapy, and long-term prognosis
recommendations.rationale: ACE-I and beta-blockers should be continued indefinitely in the presence of LV dysfunction (LVEF <40%). This 67F post-NSTEMI requires echocardiography to determine LVEF and guide long-term therapy decisions.

recommendations.intervention: Lipid profile (TC, LDL-C, HDL-C, TG) — baseline assessment for lipid management target and statin therapy monitoring
recommendations.rationale: Target LDL-C < 2.0 mmol/l for secondary prevention. This 67F with T2DM and NSTEMI requires lipid profiling to guide statin intensity.

recommendations.intervention: HbA1c — glycaemic assessment for T2DM management post-discharge
recommendations.rationale: Blood sugars should be kept less than 8mmol/l in the acute setting and then aim for optimal control following discharge. This 67F with T2DM post-NSTEMI requires HbA1c for ongoing glycaemic management.

recommendations.intervention: Serum creatinine and eGFR — baseline renal function assessment for drug dosing (metformin, ACE-I, contrast nephropathy risk post-PCI)
recommendations.rationale: Drug doses should be adjusted according to renal function. Creatinine clearance should be calculated to enable appropriate drug dosing. This 67F with T2DM is at higher risk of contrast nephropathy post-PCI.

recommendations.intervention: Radial artery access — preferred vascular access strategy for PCI even during therapeutic anticoagulation (INR 2–3) in this anticoagulated AF patient
recommendations.rationale: An uninterrupted strategy of OAC is preferred, and radial access should be used as the first choice in anticoagulated patients. In anticoagulated patients at very high risk of thrombo-embolism, uninterrupted therapy with VKA as the preferred strategy and radial access used as a first choice even during therapeutic anticoagulation (INR 2–3).

recommendations.intervention: Lifestyle modification including reduced caloric intake, regular moderate-to-vigorous physical activity ≥150 minutes/week, and smoking cessation — important CV risk reduction measures
recommendations.rationale: Lifestyle modification, weight management and increased physical activity are important measures in T2DM with coronary heart disease. Smoking cessation is strongly recommended as a high priority.

recommendations.intervention: Diet — low cholesterol, low saturated fat diet for secondary CV prevention
recommendations.rationale: Dietary modification to low cholesterol or low saturated fat diet is recommended for secondary prevention in this 67F with T2DM and NSTEMI.

recommendations.intervention: Gastric protection with proton pump inhibitor — should be considered during triple antithrombotic therapy to reduce GI bleeding risk
recommendations.rationale: Table 13 footnote states 'Gastric protection with a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) should be considered where necessary.' This 67F on triple therapy (warfarin + aspirin + clopidogrel) is at increased GI bleeding risk and warrants PPI consideration.

recommendations.intervention: Beta-blocker (e.g. Metoprolol, starting 25 mg BD, target 100 mg BD, or Bisoprolol, starting 1.25 mg daily, target 10 mg daily) orally — early administration post-NSTEMI unless contraindicated; continued indefinitely if ischaemia or LV dysfunction present
recommendations.rationale: In the absence of contraindications, beta-blockers should be administered early post-NSTEMI and continued indefinitely if ischaemia is present or in the presence of LV dysfunction (LVEF <40%).
contraindications_checked: No documented contraindications (no history of bronchial asthma, AV block, or cardiogenic shock noted)

monitoring.schedule: Weekly until stable on triple therapy, then at least monthly during triple therapy; return to routine monitoring once aspirin discontinued
monitoring.target: INR 2.0–2.5 during triple therapy; INR 2.0–3.0 (target 2.5) after transition to dual therapy

monitoring.schedule: At baseline and 4–12 weeks after statin initiation, then annually
Every 3 months until at target, then every 6 months
Baseline, 2–4 weeks after ACE-I initiation or dose change, then at least annually; more frequently if eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m²
During acute admission — keep blood sugars less than 8 mmol/l; post-discharge ongoing monitoring per T2DM management
monitoring.target: Less than 8 mmol/l in acute setting

red_flags: INR >3.5 — increased risk of intracranial haemorrhage; urgent review of warfarin dose
Signs of major bleeding (haematemesis, melaena, intracranial haemorrhage symptoms) — stop antiplatelet agents, urgent assessment
Stent thrombosis symptoms (recurrent chest pain, ECG changes) — emergency re-evaluation and consideration of urgent angiography
Systolic BP <90 mmHg — withhold beta-blocker and nitrate therapy, seek urgent review
Severe hypoglycaemia during acute admission — adjust insulin/glycaemic management
Elevated serum creatinine ≥30% from baseline or eGFR reduction ≥25% after ACE-I initiation — consider dose reduction or discontinuation
follow_up: 1–3 months: reassess triple therapy duration based on bleeding risk (HAS-BLED score); if low bleeding risk, continue triple therapy up to 6 months; if high bleeding risk, transition earlier to VKA + clopidogrel dual therapy

3–6 months: discontinue aspirin if on DES with low-to-intermediate bleeding risk; transition to long-term VKA (INR 2.0–3.0) + clopidogrel 75 mg daily — action if not done: review antithrombotic strategy
6–12 months: review need for continued dual antiplatelet therapy with VKA; reassess coronary stent status if symptoms recur

Post 12 months: in patients with stable vascular disease (>1 year, no acute events), VKA monotherapy may be considered and concomitant antiplatelet therapy should not be prescribed in absence of subsequent cardiovascular event
Ongoing: repeat INR monitoring weekly/monthly depending on stability; lipid profile and HbA1c per standard T2DM and secondary prevention follow-up
Ongoing: cardiac rehabilitation program — Phase 2 (early outpatient within 3–6 months) and Phase 3 (beyond 1 year)
unresolved_questions: Specific DES type (sirolimus-, everolimus-, or paclitaxel-eluting) not specified — triple therapy duration guidance differs: at least 3 months for sirolimus-eluting stent and at least 6 months for paclitaxel-eluting stent per CPG AF Management §6.4.3 [chunk 2]
Patient weight not specified — prasugrel is not recommended in patients <60 kg due to bleeding risk (CPG UA/NSTEMI §7.2.2.1 [chunk 13])
LV ejection fraction not documented — determines need for indefinite beta-blocker and ACE-I therapy
HAS-BLED bleeding risk score not calculated — required to stratify haemorrhagic risk and guide duration of triple therapy
Renal function (eGFR/CrCl) not provided — needed for metformin dosing, ACE-I initiation, and contrast nephropathy risk assessment post-PCI

Specific CPG publication date for the AF management guideline not clearly stated in retrieved chunks — if CPG is >5 years old, newer evidence (e.g. WOEST, PIONEER AF-PCI, RE-DUAL PCI, AUGUSTUS trials) may alter the triple therapy recommendation toward OAC + single antiplatelet

The retrieved evidence does not address DOAC-based antithrombotic strategies post-PCI in AF patients (e.g. low-dose rivaroxaban + P2Y12 inhibitor per PIONEER AF-PCI, or dabigatran + P2Y12 inhibitor per RE-DUAL PCI) — newer evidence may be preferred over VKA-based triple therapy
Blood glucose level at admission not provided — this is a significant predictor of 1-year mortality in diabetics with ACS (CPG UA/NSTEMI §9.4 [chunk 1])
No specific evidence grade available for PPI co-prescription during triple therapy — the recommendation is based on a Table footnote rather than a graded recommendation

Expected referral not surfaced in plan: Cardiology — acute coronary syndrome / NSTEMI requires invasive risk stratification. No referral recommendation was emitted — clinician should arrange specialist input.

recommendations.rationale: An uninterrupted strategy of OAC is preferred, and radial access should be used as the first choice in anticoagulated patients. In anticoagulated patients at very high risk of thrombo-embolism, uninterrupted therapy with VKA as the preferred strategy and radial access used as a first choice even during therapeutic anticoagulation (INR 2–3).

recommendations.intervention: Lifestyle modification including reduced caloric intake, regular moderate-to-vigorous physical activity ≥150 minutes/week, and smoking cessation — important CV risk reduction measures
recommendations.rationale: Lifestyle modification, weight management and increased physical activity are important measures in T2DM with coronary heart disease. Smoking cessation is strongly recommended as a high priority.

recommendations.intervention: Diet — low cholesterol, low saturated fat diet for secondary CV prevention
recommendations.rationale: Dietary modification to low cholesterol or low saturated fat diet is recommended for secondary prevention in this 67F with T2DM and NSTEMI.

recommendations.intervention: Gastric protection with proton pump inhibitor — should be considered during triple antithrombotic therapy to reduce GI bleeding risk
recommendations.rationale: Table 13 footnote states 'Gastric protection with a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) should be considered where necessary.' This 67F on triple therapy (warfarin + aspirin + clopidogrel) is at increased GI bleeding risk and warrants PPI consideration.

recommendations.intervention: Beta-blocker (e.g. Metoprolol, starting 25 mg BD, target 100 mg BD, or Bisoprolol, starting 1.25 mg daily, target 10 mg daily) orally — early administration post-NSTEMI unless contraindicated; continued indefinitely if ischaemia or LV dysfunction present
recommendations.rationale: In the absence of contraindications, beta-blockers should be administered early post-NSTEMI and continued indefinitely if ischaemia is present or in the presence of LV dysfunction (LVEF <40%).
contraindications_checked: No documented contraindications (no history of bronchial asthma, AV block, or cardiogenic shock noted)

monitoring.schedule: Weekly until stable on triple therapy, then at least monthly during triple therapy; return to routine monitoring once aspirin discontinued
monitoring.target: INR 2.0–2.5 during triple therapy; INR 2.0–3.0 (target 2.5) after transition to dual therapy

monitoring.schedule: At baseline and 4–12 weeks after statin initiation, then annually
Every 3 months until at target, then every 6 months
Baseline, 2–4 weeks after ACE-I initiation or dose change, then at least annually; more frequently if eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m²
During acute admission — keep blood sugars less than 8 mmol/l; post-discharge ongoing monitoring per T2DM management
monitoring.target: Less than 8 mmol/l in acute setting

red_flags: INR >3.5 — increased risk of intracranial haemorrhage; urgent review of warfarin dose
Signs of major bleeding (haematemesis, melaena, intracranial haemorrhage symptoms) — stop antiplatelet agents, urgent assessment
Stent thrombosis symptoms (recurrent chest pain, ECG changes) — emergency re-evaluation and consideration of urgent angiography
Systolic BP <90 mmHg — withhold beta-blocker and nitrate therapy, seek urgent review
Severe hypoglycaemia during acute admission — adjust insulin/glycaemic management
Elevated serum creatinine ≥30% from baseline or eGFR reduction ≥25% after ACE-I initiation — consider dose reduction or discontinuation
follow_up: 1–3 months: reassess triple therapy duration based on bleeding risk (HAS-BLED score); if low bleeding risk, continue triple therapy up to 6 months; if high bleeding risk, transition earlier to VKA + clopidogrel dual therapy

3–6 months: discontinue aspirin if on DES with low-to-intermediate bleeding risk; transition to long-term VKA (INR 2.0–3.0) + clopidogrel 75 mg daily — action if not done: review antithrombotic strategy
6–12 months: review need for continued dual antiplatelet therapy with VKA; reassess coronary stent status if symptoms recur

Post 12 months: in patients with stable vascular disease (>1 year, no acute events), VKA monotherapy may be considered and concomitant antiplatelet therapy should not be prescribed in absence of subsequent cardiovascular event
Ongoing: repeat INR monitoring weekly/monthly depending on stability; lipid profile and HbA1c per standard T2DM and secondary prevention follow-up
Ongoing: cardiac rehabilitation program — Phase 2 (early outpatient within 3–6 months) and Phase 3 (beyond 1 year)

Patient weight not specified — prasugrel is not recommended in patients <60 kg due to bleeding risk (CPG UA/NSTEMI §7.2.2.1 [chunk 13])
LV ejection fraction not documented — determines need for indefinite beta-blocker and ACE-I therapy
HAS-BLED bleeding risk score not calculated — required to stratify haemorrhagic risk and guide duration of triple therapy
Renal function (eGFR/CrCl) not provided — needed for metformin dosing, ACE-I initiation, and contrast nephropathy risk assessment post-PCI

Specific CPG publication date for the AF management guideline not clearly stated in retrieved chunks — if CPG is >5 years old, newer evidence (e.g. WOEST, PIONEER AF-PCI, RE-DUAL PCI, AUGUSTUS trials) may alter the triple therapy recommendation toward OAC + single antiplatelet

The retrieved evidence does not address DOAC-based antithrombotic strategies post-PCI in AF patients (e.g. low-dose rivaroxaban + P2Y12 inhibitor per PIONEER AF-PCI, or dabigatran + P2Y12 inhibitor per RE-DUAL PCI) — newer evidence may be preferred over VKA-based triple therapy
Blood glucose level at admission not provided — this is a significant predictor of 1-year mortality in diabetics with ACS (CPG UA/NSTEMI §9.4 [chunk 1])
No specific evidence grade available for PPI co-prescription during triple therapy — the recommendation is based on a Table footnote rather than a graded recommendation
